items.author: Ben (2026-09-11, Exploration design session); Claude (written into EXPLORATION.md)
items.title: Spend is estimated once at 1960 and seeds the campaign's depletion reserve
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-11): "For depletion accounting, I would prefer if we retrofit this, and come to a sensible estimate at the very end of digitisation. For generation you are right in that keeping items abstract is best policy." So NO ACCUMULATOR IS ADDED anywhere in the history sim, and sprint 39's closed Empire span is NOT reopened.

WHY IT MATTERS. Ben, 2026-09-11, on what digitisation passes forward: "the main levers we pass are going to be about how much of easily accessible resource has been actually spent." The saturated corporate web forms around what is LEFT.

WHERE IT LANDS IS ALREADY BUILT, AND THIS IS THE ELEGANT PART. `tile_component::resource_remaining` (components.hpp) is a finite reserve, live, drawn down by extraction and tapering output as it empties -- and it is SEEDED AT GENERATION to richness x a reserve factor (tile_generation.cpp). The two economy phases set that seed instead of a constant. Ground worked for centuries hands the campaign a thinner reserve. No new field, no new accumulator, no change to the campaign's extraction loop.

THE PRICE OF RETROFITTING, STATED PLAINLY AND ACCEPTED. An estimate computed once at 1960 can NEVER BE CHECKED against what actually happened, because nothing recorded it. That makes it a STATED FORMULA rather than a measurement. THE FORMULA MUST THEREFORE BE WRITTEN DOWN AS ONE -- named inputs, named arithmetic, in DIGITISATION.md -- or it silently becomes a fudge factor nobody can audit. Writing it down IS the work; an unwritten estimate is the failure mode.

ITS INPUTS ARE THE ABSTRACT ONES THE SIM ALREADY HOLDS: how long ground was held and worked, its `dominant` region class, whether it industrialised and when, and the corridor throughput that ran off it (BL-940).

PARKED UNTIL DIGITISATION IS DESIGNED. DIGITISATION.md is a placeholder by Ben's ruling; this item is filed now so the decision is not lost, and it is NOT sprint 40 work.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised)
items.title: A speed control (45s / 90s / 180s) on every lapse round's time-lapse, default 90 seconds
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13: time-lapses currently run too fast to observe what is happening. Target the FULL playback (start year to end year, unskipped) at 90 seconds by default, and add a speed-control element present in EVERY lapse round (Culture, Empires, and the new Exploration round from BL-946) offering three settings: 45 seconds, 90 seconds, 180 seconds -- the user can also already skip ahead or scrub via the existing playhead/scrubber, this control is about the AUTOPLAY rate, not a replacement for scrubbing.

WHERE THE RATE LIVES TODAY. Find whatever currently drives year-per-frame or year-per-second in `history_lapse.cpp`'s playback (a fixed constant, most likely) and make it a function of (span length in years) / (chosen duration in seconds), recomputed whenever the round's span or the chosen duration changes -- a round with a longer span at the same duration setting must move faster per frame, not take longer wall-clock time, since the target is WALL-CLOCK duration, not years-per-second.

THE CONTROL ITSELF. Three-way selector (45s / 90s / 180s), same visual language as other wizard toggles (Sparse/Lean/Standard on the main menu is the nearest precedent for a three-way radio-style control). Persisted per-session is fine; it does not need to survive a restart unless that's trivial. Update `docs/ai/ACTIONS.json` for the new control and `docs/ui/question_log.json` for the surface it lives on.

DONE WHEN: all three lapse rounds (Culture, Empires, Exploration) expose the same speed control; selecting 45s/90s/180s visibly changes the playback rate; the default is 90s; a live click confirms the control is reachable and does what it says.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-13, live review); Claude (itemised from NR-855)
items.title: Push the near/far cost split further so the displacement reading reliably clears its own bar
items.design:
BEN, 2026-09-13, resolving NR-855: push further rather than accept 0.88 as the resting state. BL-941's deterrence (Ceiling/Alarm at polity grain, wired into `treaty_value_q`'s near-home Alarm bonus and a flat `treaty_far_penalty_q` for distant pairs) moved the median displacement ratio from 0.01/0.16 up to 0.88 across a 3-seed sweep -- real progress, one seed already cleared 1.0, but the median has not. Strengthen the SAME mechanism rather than inventing a second one: widen the gap between the near-home Alarm bonus and the far-away penalty (both already exist in history_sim.cpp from BL-941), and/or extend Alarm's read of visible capability (standing army + navy) to weight more heavily on a longer-held border. Re-sweep at a WIDER seed count (16, not 3, per NR-855's own note that 3 seeds was chosen for runtime, not confidence) before judging the reading settled either way.

Do not touch the non-aggression block itself (BL-933) or the ratio's own definition (BL-948's operationalisation, confirmed correct by Ben 2026-09-13) -- this item is about the deterrence STRENGTH, not the measurement or the blocking mechanism.

DONE WHEN: a 16-seed sweep shows the median displacement ratio clears 1.0, conflict still persists (reading 2 stays green -- total conflict well above zero), and the change is a measured strengthening of BL-941's existing mechanism, not a new one bolted on.

PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (NR-862, bisected). The 0.88 starting point was a 3-seed median resting on one seed. The wave-4 tree over 16 seeds read 0.33; the schism verb (BL-944) then cut it to 0.08 at HEAD. Sprint 41 wave 1 (trade flows, outward wants, the handoff) moves it again. Tune from the 16-seed reading on the INTEGRATED sprint-41 tree, record that baseline first (requirement R2), and look at why the schism collapses frontier war on some seeds before widening the deterrence gap.

SPRINT 41 WAVE 3 (2026-09-14, merged 41e2f5c7): Alarm weight 575, far penalty 700 -> 16-seed median displacement 1.34 (0.08 before the sprint), battle rate 44.8 per century; seeds 0, 3, 9, 14 fall under 5 battles per century. R1 and R2 complete. OPEN: R3, Ben's authorisation of the wave's world shape (NR-867). The item closes when that lands, at 575 or at the alternative 525.

items.author: Claude (sprint 41 T2 finding, BL-956)
items.title: world_determinism digest covers seeded sentiment and stamped road tiers
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-14 by sprint 41 T2 (BL-956, Exploration handoff crosses). BL-956 moved world setup from 1200 CE grudges and corridors to 1660 ones: on seed ABCDEF01 sentiment seeding went from the 1200 grudge set to 76 rows off 225 grudges, and stamped corridors from 1664 to 2276 (612 new). Every world_determinism digest stayed digit-identical, because the digest reads neither `world::sentiment` nor road tiers. A contract that cannot see a change of that size is the same defect memory records for trade (goldens cannot see convoy traffic): the determinism check proves same-seed-same-world only for the parts it hashes.

WORK: fold seeded sentiment (sorted pairs and values) and the road tier per tile (or a per-tier tile count per body) into the deep digest. This moves every digest once: per DELIVERY.md sec The digest re-bless is one act per WAVE it is an authorised re-bless with the movement described (what the digest now covers), in its own commit, never folded into a world-moving item.

DONE WHEN: world_determinism fails when sentiment seeding or road stamping changes (demonstrate by a deliberate one-row perturbation run locally, not committed), and the re-bless is authorised by Ben.

items.author: Claude (sprint 41 wave 3 finding, BL-949)
items.title: The Empires span's try_upgrade_corridor writes its promotion into the corridor record
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-14 by sprint 41 wave 3 (BL-949, road rung fires). The Exploration span's post road set the live use count to the tier threshold but appended one row to the corridor record, so the record under-read the tier; BL-949 fixed it by carrying `history_corridor::tier`. `try_upgrade_corridor` in the EMPIRES span has the same one-row shape: the carried tier is now right, but `uses` still under-reads for any consumer that reads traffic rather than tier. Not fixed in sprint 41 because it moves the 1960/two-span digest, which the sprint kept unchanged by design.

WORK: make the Empires promotion write its uses consistently with the tier it grants (or document `uses` as traffic-only and audit every reader to use `tier`). Report the 1960 and seedA/off digest movement; re-bless only with authorisation.
